scope: Verification of the reference tool's explicit sRGB host-CPU storage convention option (--srgb-host-convention encoded|linear) for the Vapor Vulkan wrapper. The patched candidate build (tools/vulkan-wrapper/srgb-storage.patch) linearises BC*_SRGB texels in the host bcdec fallback like the compute shaders, so it must be compared against the linearised reference; the unpatched baseline must still fail under 'linear' (negative control) and the pinned unpatched candidate must keep passing under the default 'encoded' convention. Offscreen transfer-only emulator probe; no app, phone/Adreno or CI result is claimed.
label: srgb-expectation

option.name: --srgb-host-convention

values.encoded: host-CPU bcdec fallback stores sRGB-encoded numeric values (pinned/unpatched builds; default, keeps earlier receipts reproducible)
values.linear: host-CPU bcdec fallback linearises sRGB texels (patched build carrying tools/vulkan-wrapper/srgb-storage.patch)

option.host_cpu_tolerance: 0 LSB expected for the matching convention; the compute/native comparisons are unchanged

fixture_source_rule_summary: BC1/DXT1 block is 8 bytes: RGB565 c0, RGB565 c1 (little-endian), then 16 2-bit indices, LSB first, row-major inside the 4x4 block.
Endpoint components are UNORM: c/31 (red, blue) and c/63 (green) expanded to 8-bit with round-to-nearest.
c0 > c1: palette is [c0, c1, (2c0+c1)/3, (c0+2c1)/3]. Else: [c0, c1, (c0+c1)/2, transparent black (0,0,0,0)].
BC3/DXT5 block is 16 bytes: 8-byte alpha block, then an 8-byte BC1 colour block that ALWAYS uses the four-colour palette regardless of c0 vs c1.

All palette interpolants are exact rational weighted averages scaled to 8-bit and rounded to nearest with ties to even, the Vulkan/D3D float-to-UNORM convention. This is the convention the wrapper's compute-shader decoder implements; the emulator runs match it exactly (including a 42.5 tie that resolves to 42 on the driver).

BC4_UNORM/BC5_UNORM (RGTC): a BC4 block is 8 bytes = 8-bit endpoints a0/a1 then 16 3-bit indices, LSB first; the palette is identical to the BC3 alpha palette (8 entries when a0 > a1, otherwise 6 interpolated entries plus 0 and 255). BC5 is 16 bytes: a red BC4-like block followed by a green BC4-like block (red at bytes 0-7, green at bytes 8-15), decoding to (r,g).

Wrapper storage convention for emulated BC formats: the wrapper replaces BC1/BC2/BC3/BC4/BC5/BC7 images with R8G8B8A8_UNORM and expands BC4 to (r,r,r,255) and BC5 to (r,g,0,255); this tool compares against that documented convention for the wrapper copy paths and against the native uncompressed channel data for the driver blit-decode path.

sRGB BC1/BC3: the wrapper compute-shader decode linearises sRGB texels before storing them in the emulated R8G8B8A8_UNORM image, while the host-CPU (bcdec) fallback stores the sRGB-encoded numeric values without linearisation. The tool compares each wrapper decode path against its matching reference (linearised for compute/compute-view, encoded for host-cpu) and records the convention and the observed disagreement between the two paths.

BC2/BC6/BC7 decoding is not implemented in the independent reference; BC7 format support is still recorded from the driver. No sampling or rendering pipeline is created: decoded data is observed through buffer-image copies and vkCmdBlitImage.

reference_decoder.language: python (pure stdlib, implemented for this tool)
reference_decoder.provenance: Original implementation from the S3TC/DXT1/DXT5 block-layout and palette rules documented in the Khronos Data Format / OpenGL EXT_texture_compression_s3tc family of specifications. No wrapper, bcdec or Mesa decoder code is reused; the wrapper's bcdec and compute-shader paths are the objects under test.

cases.name: bc1 three-colour palette c0=blue c1=red (transparent index 3)
bc1 equal endpoints use three-colour mode
bc3 ignores colour endpoint order (always four-colour)
bc1 index order is LSB-first row-major
bc3 generator covers both alpha modes
d24s8 input values fit in 24 bits
bc4 block index 0 decodes to the low endpoint
bc5 interleaves a red block then a green block per 16-byte block

generators.algorithm: Python random.Random(seed); block patterns cycle through four-colour, three-colour/transparent, equal-endpoint, all-black/all-white and random BC1/BC3 blocks so every palette branch and index range is exercised

limitations: Software Vulkan only: the emulator runs on llvmpipe (LLVMpipe) inside the Android emulator, not on Adreno/KGSL and not on a physical GPU.
No phone is attached to the qualifying machine. No Adreno, KGSL or physical-GPU result is claimed; the phone runbook is written but not executed.
Synthetic deterministic BC blocks, not game assets; no mip levels, array layers, sRGB variants or sub-block partial copies are exercised.
No graphics pipeline is created: the wrapper's decoded image is observed through buffer-image copies (and vkCmdBlitImage for the native driver decode), not through sampling or rendering.
No validation layers are loaded; correctness relies on probe metrics, not API validation.
BC7 decoding is not implemented in the independent reference; only BC7 format support is recorded. BC2/4/5/6 are likewise not part of the reference comparison.

Interpolated BC palette entries legitimately differ by a few LSBs between decoder implementations; the wrapper compute path matches the reference exactly, the wrapper CPU fallback (bcdec) is within 1 LSB and Mesa's native decoder within 2 LSB on this run, which is why a tolerance is reported alongside exact counts.
The pinned wrapper is a build-tree .so loaded via dlopen by the probe; it is not packaged, installed or selected by Vapor in this run.

Depth format reduction (WRAPPER_REDUCE_DEPTH_FORMAT) was deliberately not exercised: the required gate is create/bind/copy through TRANSFER_DST|TRANSFER_SRC, so depth images do not request DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT usage.

BC7 reference independence caveat: the reference decoder is bcdec (pinned wrapper source, bcdec.h), which is ALSO the wrapper's host-CPU fallback decoder; the host-cpu results are a self-consistency check, while the wrapper compute-shader bc7.comp and llvmpipe's native BC7 decoder are independent implementations and are the meaningful differential comparisons.
